subject: Commitment variance: evaluation window alignment & go-live validation
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment variance: evaluation window alignment & go-live validation

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Quick update from our side — we’ve been working through the SOC2 packaging and the security team surfaced an additional set of evidence items that will take roughly 2–3 business weeks to collect and redact. I attached the SOC2 evidence checklist so you can see the delta.

Given that, our legal/procurement team intends to hold signature until the security package is in a final state. That pushes the 1 Jul go-live out; we’re estimating a 3-week slip unless we split scope.

Options we’re considering internally:
- Split go-live: core API routes first (read-only), then write/monitoring features after evidence complete
- Keep full scope but accept a 3-week delay

Can you propose a mutual action table update and an escalation path if redlines become blocking? We’re committed to this integration but need a clean audit trail for our SOC auditor.

Attaching: Nimbus-SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Director of Integrations, Nimbus Health
elena.park@nimbushealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment variance: evaluation window alignment & go-live validation

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the checklist. I reviewed with the integration team and we can mitigate the schedule hit with a phased delivery approach. Proposed immediate next steps: 

1) Phase A (target: 1 Jul) — read-only endpoints + dashboard readouts + KV-sync for 30 days (limited dataset).
   - Owners: Integration (Connor) + CS (Marissa)
2) Phase B (target: 22 Jul) — write paths, monitoring, and audit log retention once SOC2 evidence is validated.
   - Owners: Eng Release (Rishi) + Security (Laura)
3) Contract/signature: We can accept signature on the partial-scope SOW if procurement will commit in writing to remaining items and a target sign date for final SOW (we’ll accept DocuSign hold if necessary).

I attached a first-pass mutual action table (proposed_map_v2.xlsx). Key asks for your team: confirm which connectors must be live in Phase A and firm up an expected date for SOC evidence completion.

If legal redlines threaten to delay the partial SOW acceptance, we ask to trigger the escalation path below: 
- Day 5 after submission: Redwood legal lead (Laura Bennett) to engage Nimbus legal lead (cc’d) for a redline walkthrough
- Day 10: Exec sponsor-to-sponsor check-in (VP of Sales / Director of Integrations)

We can also offer a short technical sandbox (no PII) to let auditors validate controls in parallel with evidence collection.

Attaching: proposed_map_v2.xlsx

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Account Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0124

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment variance: evaluation window alignment & go-live validation

Looping in a couple of risk items from CS/Implementation perspective so we have them in the thread: 

- SSO (Okta) config: we still need the test tenant credentials and metadata; without that Phase A cannot validate user mapping (owner: Nimbus SSO team).
- Dataset ingestion validation: we need a small gold dataset and schema confirmation (owner: Nimbus Data Eng).
- Payment gateway certs for billing route (owner: Nimbus Finance / Gateway vendor).

If procurement is pausing signature, we should still lock down the non-legal blockers so Phase A can proceed as soon as signature is acceptable. From a commercial standpoint, if the signature shift causes a measurable go-live revenue delay, I’m prepared to recommend a 2-week service credit to keep the relationship positive — I’ll discuss with sales ops but want to flag as a leverage option.

Also — recommend we schedule a weekly 30-minute MAP standup (Wednesdays) and a decision-owner list in the MAP to avoid repeated triage emails.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment variance: evaluation window alignment & go-live validation

Thanks, everyone — the phased approach sounds workable. A few confirmations from our side:

- Procurement: they will not sign the final SOW until the SOC2 evidence packet is complete; legal estimates ~10 business days to finish redline resolution once we provide the requested artifacts (I attached the redlines summary).
- Phase A scope: Elena confirms read-only + dashboard accepted for initial rollout; we will provide the gold dataset and SSO test metadata by Tue next week.
- Escalation: if redlines are not concluded in 10 business days post-submission, please escalate to your legal lead and we’ll escalate internally to our VP of Integrations.

Elena — can you please update proposed_map_v2.xlsx with the specific `decision-owner` column and the planned dates for the artifacts you mentioned? Once we have that, Marissa and Rishi, can you confirm the weekly MAP standup cadence and the exec escalation contact?

Attaching: redlines_0624.pdf

Best,
Elena Park
Director of Integrations, Nimbus Health
